biography.plain_text: Eugene Shvidler is a Soviet-born British-American investor whose fortune began in oil. After emigrating to the United States and working at Deloitte, he entered business with longtime friend Roman Abramovich, co-founded the Runicom trading operation and became a Millhouse shareholder. The sale of Millhouse's controlling Sibneft stake became the basis of his subsequent investment holdings.

long_biography.plain_text:
Board roles at Evraz and Highland Gold Mining placed Eugene Shvidler inside the governance of two major resource businesses after his oil career. He acquired a personal stake in Evraz at its initial public offering and later joined the steelmaker's board; at Highland Gold, he combined ownership with executive chairmanship. His training in applied mathematics and corporate finance supported a role spanning board oversight, asset management and capital allocation.

Education and painting have given Shvidler a public presence outside resource investing. His support helped establish Fordham University's Center for Jewish Studies, extending a connection to the university where he completed graduate business and taxation degrees. Under the name ES23, he brought an artistic practice begun in childhood into public view through exhibitions of abstract painting.
